message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the presence of a mane in adult male individuals. The allele responsible for mane growth (often linked to the *SRD5A2* gene and its regulation) is dominant over the allele that results in a lack of mane. Thus, when a male lion inherits the mane allele from either parent, it will typically develop a full mane.
